Link radar, September 9, 2026

Frontier labs and infra providers shipped a dense day of primary-source reading on September 8: a machine-checked mathematics proof produced by a very large agent run, a faster image generation model with new editing controls, a petabyte-scale catalogue of human DNA variant effects, post-quantum origin handshakes rolling out across billions of daily connections, and centrally managed sandboxes for coding assistants in IDEs. Each summary below is in our own words; follow the links for the originals.

Signal, not noise: five primary-source reads published September 8, each with a two-line note on why it matters for builders.

On the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem

A very large agent run produced a machine-checked singularity proof in about eighty-eight hours plus seventeen hours of formalization. It is a useful real-world template for large multi-agent orchestration, cross-group consolidation, and machine-checked output receipts.

Read the full story at OpenAI (September 8, 2026).

Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5

A new image model promises up to fifty percent lower latency with stronger reference fidelity, plus two API models with a default and a premium tier. It is directly actionable for product image workflows: targeted edits that preserve identity plus sketch, template, and comment-on-image controls.

Read the full story at OpenAI (September 8, 2026).

AlphaGenome Atlas: Molecular predictions for 9 Billion human DNA variants

A one-petabyte precomputed catalogue covers all nine billion single-letter variant effects with a single ranking score plus an API and an assistant skill. It is a good reference for exposing huge model outputs as a zero-code portal plus API, and for ranking candidates before expensive lab validation.

Read the full story at Google DeepMind (September 8, 2026).

Automatic Key Exchange: faster, post-quantum secure origin handshakes for 45 billion daily connections (and counting)

The post describes probing origins then leading with the strongest key agreement, preferring a post-quantum hybrid, with handshake retries down sharply and tail latency down more than one hundred fifty milliseconds. Infra builders can copy the pattern: measure capability out of band, roll out per origin with rollback, and rescan daily for upgrades.

Read the full story at Cloudflare (September 8, 2026).

Enterprise-managed sandbox in Copilot for JetBrains

Admins can now centrally enforce sandbox enablement plus filesystem, network, proxy, and tool access, with locked IDE controls and diagnostics. It is a practical baseline for teams running coding agents in IDEs: managed boundaries plus command-line to IDE context linking without handing over the machine.

Read the full story at GitHub (September 8, 2026).
